newsitem.title: USA: US rail carloads, ton-miles off from yr ago - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail carloads, ton-miles off from yr ago - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in carloads and ton-miles fell sharply in the week ended September 14 from the same week in 1996 due to hurricane-related weather conditions, a railroad group said Thursday in a statement.
The Association of American Railroads reported 348,188 carloads in the week, down 5.9 percent from 370,081 in the year-ago week.
AAR said ton-miles fell 5.1 percent to 26.0 billion in the week from 27.4 billion last year. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
But intermodal traffic, which does not include carloads, totaled 167,635 trailers and containers, up 3.9 percent from 161,302 a year ago.

"In addition to problems associated with weather, the continued weakness in grain loadings also contributed to the decline," AAR chief economist Harvey Levine said. Grain carloads totaled 18,800 in the week, a 34.2 percent plunge from 28,576 last year.
Loadings of metallic ores also fell 18.1 percent to 17,977 from 21,942 a year ago, along with farm products other than grain, which were off 11.3 percent to 942 carloads from 1,062 last year.
Loadings of lumber and wood products stood at 5,635, down 2.3 percent from 5,767 in the year-ago week. Motor vehicles and equipment also dipped 1.1 percent to 21,754 carloads from 21,993, AAR said.
But petroleum products were up 4.1 percent to 5,931 carloads from 5,696 a year ago. Metals and products rose 7.3 percent to 12,907 carloads from 12,029 in the same 1996 week.
In the first 37 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose 2.0 percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic was up 0.6 percent, but carloads fell 0.9 percent, AAR said.
